title: Host pipeline: microbatch-driven kernel adapter and CPU-side coalescing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce host-side CPU overhead and memory-copy spikes by introducing a microbatch-driven kernel adapter that selects kernels based on observed per-request sequence length distributions and by implementing a CPU coalescing layer that reuses pinned buffers and flattens memcpy bursts. Goal: cut tail p95 host-CPU usage and reduce prefill->decode latency spikes without increasing median GPU queue latency.
acceptance_criteria: P95 host CPU utilization for a 500req/s mixed-length workload decreases by >= 25% compared to current baseline
Frequency and magnitude of memcpy spikes (as measured by host memcopy time per-second) reduced by >= 60%
No degradation > 5% in median GPU tokens/sec throughput for long-sequence workloads
Integration tests for kernel adapter logic added and passing in CI; feature flagged behind runtime.experimental.microbatch_adapter
Benchmark harness (kbench) updated with mixed-length trace and reproducible perf dashboard link
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: RFC created. Motivation: observed memcopy spikes and threadpool contention when many short prefill requests interleave with long-decoding requests on same host. Proposed approach: 1) microbatch aggregator on host that groups short prefills for shared pinned buffer usage; 2) kernel adapter that picks 'fast-path' kernels for short sequences and falls back to high-throughput kernels for long sequences; 3) adaptive threadpool backpressure for decode stage.

2026-02-16 Marco Rodrigues: Spike analysis attached (link). Short traces (<=64 tokens) cause many tiny pinned allocations and synchronous cudaMemcpy calls that thrash the host allocator. Measured 72% of memcpy time came from allocations. Experimented with persistent pinned pool and saw 35% reduction locally.

2026-02-19 Leah Kim (review): Design looks promising. Request to clarify correctness for KV cache lifetimes when microbatching across requests that might time out or cancel. Added follow-up task to ensure per-request ownership and zero-copy token boundaries.

2026-02-22 Marco Rodrigues: Implemented MVP: pinned buffer pool + microbatch aggregator. Feature flag runtime.experimental.microbatch_adapter behind kbench experiments. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1327. Local perf: p95 host CPU down 28%, memcpy spikes down 52%.

2026-02-26 Performance note: Need kernel selection hysteresis to avoid oscillation when sequence length distribution shifts rapidly. Added soft TTL for kernel picks (default 10s) and a tiny performance probe to test candidate kernels with a single warmup iteration.

2026-03-02 Marco Rodrigues: Added adaptive threadpool policy: worker counts scale with aggregate pending decode tokens, not requests. This reduced thread wakeups by ~40% on synthetic mix and reduced context-switches in perf samples.

2026-03-07 Security review (Seth Nguyen): Ensure pinned pool is zeroed before reuse to avoid cross-tenant leakage. Action item added to zero buffers on free and add KMS key restriction verification for private deployments.

2026-03-10 Marco Rodrigues: Running full canary in staging with runtime-1.22. Initial 24h run: p95 host CPU -30%, memcpy burst events from 23/day -> 6/day. Observed minor increase (~3%) in median GPU kernel launches for long sequences due to adapter probe cost — acceptable per perf guardrails. Scheduling rollback plan ready if regressions exceed thresholds.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Next steps: broaden canary, add sampled telemetry for kernel-adapter decision path, finalize docs for Console feature flag and admin toggle.
